record.context_brief: Exact distances of BCH and QR codes
record.original_question: For cyclic codes in the classical families discussed in the chapter, what are the exact minimum distances of Bose–Chaudhuri–Hocquenghem (BCH) codes and quadratic residue (QR) codes in the cases where those distances are still unknown?

evidence.quote: The minimum dis￾tance of GRM codes is known (see comments of Section 3.2 and 3.4.1). This is generally not known for BCH codes and QR codes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let q be a prime power and n a positive integer with gcd(n,q)=1. A cyclic code C of length n over the finite field F_q is an ideal in F_q[x]/(x^n-1), generated by a divisor g(x) of x^n-1; equivalently, C is specified by its set of zeros (the "defining set") among the n-th roots of unity in an extension of F_q. The minimum distance d(C) of C is the smallest Hamming weight of a nonzero codeword in C.

Two classical families:
(1) BCH codes. Fix a primitive n-th root of unity α in an extension of F_q, a "designed distance" δ with 2 ≤ δ ≤ n, and an integer b ≥ 0. The BCH code BCH_q(n,δ,b) is the cyclic code over F_q whose defining set contains {α^{b}, α^{b+1}, …, α^{b+δ-2}}; that is, its generator polynomial is the least-degree monic divisor of x^n−1 over F_q having these elements as zeros. The BCH bound gives d(BCH_q(n,δ,b)) ≥ δ, but the exact value of d is in general not known.
(2) Quadratic residue (QR) codes. Let p be an odd prime such that q is a quadratic residue mod p, and let Q ⊂ (Z/pZ)^* be the set of nonzero quadratic residues mod p. Let β be a primitive p-th root of unity in an extension of F_q. The (binary or q-ary) quadratic residue codes of length p are the cyclic codes over F_q with generator polynomials ∏_{i∈Q}(x−β^i) and ∏_{i∈Q∪{0}}(x−β^i), together with their counterparts using the set of nonresidues. The exact minimum distances of these codes are known in only finitely many cases.

Problem. Determine, in closed form or by an effective rule, the exact minimum distance d(C) of every BCH code BCH_q(n,δ,b) and of every quadratic residue code of prime length p over F_q, in the infinite families of parameters for which this exact value is currently unknown.
artifact.category_tag: Coding theory: minimum distance of cyclic codes
artifact.status_search_result: Determining the exact minimum distance of BCH codes and quadratic residue codes is widely regarded as a hard open problem. Recent works (e.g., a 2025 Springer paper on BCH codes with explicit minimum distance and a 2026 arXiv preprint "On the Minimum Distances of Some Families of BCH Codes") report partial progress by settling specific infinite subfamilies, while general formulas remain unknown; the underlying minimum-distance computation is NP-hard for general linear codes, and QR codes of various lengths still have unresolved minimum distances.

status_evidence.title: On the Minimum Distances of Some Families of BCH Codes
status_evidence.snippet: Recent preprint settling further infinite families of BCH codes, indicating the general problem is still active.
status_evidence.claim: Exact minimum distances of BCH codes are determined only for specific families; the general problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: BCH codes with explicit minimum distance and applications
status_evidence.snippet: Although the BCH bound provides a lower bound on the minimum distance of BCH codes, determining the true minimum distances of BCH codes is a very challenging problem.
status_evidence.claim: Determining true minimum distances of BCH codes is an ongoing challenge with only partial results.

status_evidence.title: A New Way to Find the Minimum Distance of BCH and Quadratic Double Circulant Codes
status_evidence.snippet: For large lengths, the true value of the minimum distances of BCH and Quadratic Double Circulant codes remains undetermined.
status_evidence.claim: Minimum distances of BCH and related codes are unknown for large lengths.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on cyclic codes
status_evidence.snippet: Problem listing on cyclic codes including BCH and QR families.
status_evidence.claim: The exact minimum distances for BCH and QR codes are listed as open.
